items.title: Common Causes of Engine Misfire (Cheapest to Most Expensive)
items.description: Comprehensive cost, failure mechanics, and vehicle susceptibility analysis for UK motorists.

rows: Electrode gap widens over mileage, causing weak spark or complete spark blowout under cylinder boost pressure.
All petrol vehicles (Ford, Vauxhall, VW, BMW, Audi)
Internal coil windings break down thermally, preventing spark discharge to the plug.
Ford EcoBoost 1.0, VW/Audi TSI/TFSI, BMW N20/N55
Piezo/solenoid nozzle cokes with carbon or leaks fuel continuously into the cylinder.
Diesel common rail (Mercedes OM651, Ford DV6, BMW N47)
Split PCV breather hose or cracked manifold gasket draws unmetered air, causing extreme lean misfire.
Inert exhaust gas floods combustion chamber at idle, suffocating the flame front.
Modern diesels (VW EA189, Mercedes OM651, Ford 2.0 TDCi)
Exhaust valve face burns or warps, allowing combustion gases to leak out of the cylinder head.
High-mileage petrol turbo engines, interference valve designs
Piston compression rings stick in grooves from oil carbon or cylinder bore scoring occurs.
Combustion fire ring fails between cylinders or leaks combustion pressure directly into coolant passages.
BMW N47, Subaru Boxer, VW EA189, Mercedes OM651

items.title: 8-Step Diagnostic Process (Cheapest to Most Expensive)
items.description: Never replace costly components blindly. Follow the professional garage diagnostic ladder to pinpoint faults accurately.

rows: Reads specific freeze frame data and cylinder fault codes (P0300–P0308).
Swapping coil to adjacent cylinder verifies if misfire migrates with the coil pack.
Evaluates electrode wear, oil fouling, and verifies spark gap clearances.
Measures injector fuel return rates and spray patterns to confirm injector health.
Introduces pressurised smoke into the intake manifold to identify air leak paths.
Measures cylinder cranking pressure to identify sealing across valves and rings.
Applies compressed air into cylinder at TDC to listen where pressure escapes.
HD optical camera inspects cylinder bore walls, piston crown, and valve seats.

blocks.text: Specialist Diagnostic Rule of Thumb: On any petrol vehicle showing a single-cylinder misfire, swap the ignition coil pack with an adjacent working cylinder. If the misfire code follows the coil pack, you have confirmed a £70–£220 fix without buying guessing parts. If the misfire remains stationary, immediately proceed to compression and injector flow analysis.

blocks.text: Ford Focus 1.0 EcoBoost: How a £120 Ignition Coil Cost £1,220

A 2014 Ford Focus 1.0 EcoBoost owner observed a flashing engine management light on the A1 but decided to continue driving 15 miles home. The constant cylinder 2 misfire dumped atomised petrol directly into the catalytic converter, causing the precious metal honeycomb core to disintegrate and weld shut under extreme heat. Final Breakdown: £120 (Replacement Coil Pack) + £1,100 (New OEM Catalytic Converter & Oxygen Sensors) = £1,220 total bill . Pulling over immediately and utilizing standard breakdown recovery would have resolved the repair for just £120.

cards.title: What causes an engine to misfire? +
cards.text: The most common causes include: worn spark plugs (petrol), failed ignition coil packs (petrol), clogged, leaking, or faulty fuel injectors (petrol and diesel), unmetered vacuum air intake leaks, an EGR valve stuck open (diesel), and internal mechanical low compression (burnt valves, worn piston rings, or blown cylinder head gaskets).
cards.fullText: What causes an engine to misfire? + The most common causes include: worn spark plugs (petrol), failed ignition coil packs (petrol), clogged, leaking, or faulty fuel injectors (petrol and diesel), unmetered vacuum air intake leaks, an EGR valve stuck open (diesel), and internal mechanical low compression (burnt valves, worn piston rings, or blown cylinder head gaskets).

cards.title: Can I drive with a misfire? +
cards.text: If your engine management light is illuminated solid (not flashing) and the car operates without severe shuddering, you can drive gently to a nearby specialist garage. If the light is flashing , stop driving immediately. A flashing light signals that unburnt fuel is entering the exhaust manifold and actively melting the catalytic converter or DPF core.
cards.fullText: Can I drive with a misfire? + If your engine management light is illuminated solid (not flashing) and the car operates without severe shuddering, you can drive gently to a nearby specialist garage. If the light is flashing , stop driving immediately. A flashing light signals that unburnt fuel is entering the exhaust manifold and actively melting the catalytic converter or DPF core.

cards.title: How do I know if it's a coil or spark plug? +
cards.text: Swap the ignition coil pack from the misfiring cylinder with an adjacent working cylinder. Clear fault codes and rescan with an OBD2 tool. If the misfire fault code moves to the new cylinder, the coil pack is defective (£70–£220). If the misfire remains on the original cylinder, test the spark plug, fuel injector, and cylinder compression in order of lowest cost first.
cards.fullText: How do I know if it's a coil or spark plug? + Swap the ignition coil pack from the misfiring cylinder with an adjacent working cylinder. If the misfire remains on the original cylinder, test the spark plug, fuel injector, and cylinder compression in order of lowest cost first.

cards.text: If your vehicle has a market value of £2,000–£4,000 and the repair is an ignition coil (£70–£220) or single injector (£120–£900), fixing it is highly economical compared to purchasing a replacement vehicle. mainEntity.name: Can I drive with a misfire?

acceptedAnswer.text: If the engine management light is steady and the car runs reasonably, you can drive gently to a garage. If the light is flashing, stop driving immediately - unburnt fuel is destroying your catalytic converter (petrol) or DPF (diesel). A flashing EML is an emergency.

mainEntity.name: How do I know if it's a coil or spark plug?

acceptedAnswer.text: Swap the ignition coil from the misfiring cylinder with another cylinder. If the misfire moves to the new cylinder, the coil is bad (£70-£220). If the misfire stays on the same cylinder, it could be a spark plug, injector, or compression issue. Diagnose from cheapest to most expensive.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth fixing a misfire on an old car?

acceptedAnswer.text: If your car is worth £2,000-£4,000 and the repair is a coil (£70-£220) or injector (£120-£900), yes - a replacement car would cost far more. If the misfire is caused by low compression (valves: £800-£2,000) and the car is worth under £2,000, evaluate scrap first.

mainEntity.name: Which engines have the most misfire problems?

acceptedAnswer.text: Based on 2025 data and KNOWN FAILURE PATTERNS: Mercedes OM651 (1,250 - injector seal failure), VW/Audi EA189 (1,050 - injector coking), BMW N47 (1,450 - injector issues from chain debris), Ford DV6 (780 - injector failure). On petrol engines, VW/Audi EA888 (130 - ignition coil failure) and Ford EcoBoost (185 - coil, injector or wet belt issues). [EM-VERIFIED]
